$comment: Pricing, fee schedules, installation workflow, workforce, permitting, contract terms and company scale for a Flock deployment. Every row cites sources.json. Prices are per unit per year unless stated.

intro.headline: Pricing and cost structure
intro.summary: Flock sells the Falcon as an annual subscription and retains ownership of the hardware. Per Flock's implementation guide, the annual fee covers the camera, pole, solar panel, cellular data, cloud storage, software and installation labour. A one-time installation fee, permit costs, electrician work for AC sites, and replacement of lost, stolen or damaged equipment are billed separately. The list price changed from $2,500 to $3,000 per camera per year on 1 January 2024. The installation fee is $1,000 to $1,250 on the 2026 schedule; contracts from 2019 to 2023 list $250 to $350.

workflow.flock: Presents viable options; has final discretion on placement under the agreement
workflow.customer: Approves the deployment plan; clears it with public works

workflow.flock: Proceeds on non-permit sites; historically a ten-location minimum for a partial install
workflow.customer: Signs; starts permit applications; gets an electrician quote for AC sites

workflow.flock: 'Assists in packaging your application'; has working relationships with some DOTs such as IDOT
workflow.customer: 'Solely responsible for any permits or associated costs, and managing the permitting process'
workflow.other: DOT, public works or pole owner issues the permit

workflow.flock: Technician checks solar exposure, sight line to the road and cellular signal; flags each spot
Coordinates the call; a ten-foot radius is marked
Standard MUTCD control by the technician
workflow.customer: Provides a patrol escort or pays for full traffic control; custom plans can double the cost

workflow.flock: Field Operations technician or an approved third-party technician sets the pole, panel and camera and aims it
workflow.customer: Pays for a bucket truck when the mount is above about 15 ft

workflow.flock: Supplies the kit; verifies power remotely while the electrician is on site
workflow.customer: Hires, pays and carries liability for the electrician; must finish within two days of install

workflow.flock: Checks capture quality for seven business days, then grants full access; the contract term commences at validation
Maintains its equipment; bills moves and non-defect replacements per the fee schedule
workflow.customer: Pays for relocations, losses, electrical faults and outage downtime

workforce.v: A Field Operations team of travelling technicians, organised in at least three regions, doing new installs and maintenance about half and half; postings list $55,000 to $65,000

The agreement allows third-party labour and Flock's installer app is restricted to its technicians 'and approved third party technicians'; Gadget Review reported DISH's OnTech unit as one such installer; the split between in-house and contract work is not published
Falcon Flex is customer-installed with no on-site service; its contract term commences at signature rather than validation
Installs typically complete six to eight weeks after locations are final; permitting can add two months or more
Cameras assembled in Atlanta; a 97,000 square foot Smyrna, Georgia plant opened in 2025 for drones, panel assembly and refurbishing returned hardware

permitting.permit: Public works approval; sometimes an encroachment permit
permitting.who: Customer manages the application; Flock assists with packaging it
Customer under the agreement; Flock works with some DOTs directly
permitting.note: Cameras were installed without state approval in Florida, Illinois and South Carolina; South Carolina DOT identified 200 or more and paused new installations in 2023. Florida DOT revoked all state right-of-way permits on 31 August 2026 with 30 days for removal.

permitting.permit: Attachment agreement with the pole owner
permitting.who: Customer or Flock; not always documented
permitting.note: One telecom company stated that cameras were attached to its poles without its knowledge

permitting.permit: Breakaway or MASH-rated pole where required
permitting.note: Jalopnik reported in 2026 on poles set inside clear zones without breakaway bases

permitting.permit: Owner consent; encroachment permit if the pole meets public right of way

permitting.note: Roanoke, VA: 30 of 41 Raven audio sensors were installed at locations not on the approved list after a city data-entry error; the city later cancelled the program

contract.v: 'All Flock Hardware is owned exclusively by Flock'; the customer may not move, adjust or take possession of it, except self-installed Flex units

Contracts from 2023 and earlier specify removal within six months of termination; the 2026 terms specify 'a commercially reasonable time'. In Verona, Evanston and Cambridge, cameras were reported still in place or reinstalled after termination
One, two, five and ten-year terms exist; renewals roll automatically unless notice is given 30 days before the end
Half the year's fee plus the install fee is due up front, a quarter when installation starts, the rest on completion
An outage of a day or more extends the term by the same length, pro rata; there is no cash credit

The 'Flock does not own and shall not sell Customer Data' sentence was deleted, the data licence became perpetual and product-improvement scoped, disputes moved to Georgia arbitration, the gross-negligence carve-out left the liability cap, and the non-appropriation exit was narrowed

OMNIA, Sourcewell, Texas DIR and similar cooperative contracts provide an exemption from competitive bidding under state procurement rules; a Park Ridge sole-source memo states 'all of our neighboring communities are in the Flock system'

scale.v: More than 120,000 in 49 states per Flock; about 96,000 mapped by DeFlock contributors
More than 5,000 law-enforcement agencies and 6,000 communities per Flock; retail customers including Home Depot and Lowe's share parking-lot camera data with police searches per The American Prospect
Annual recurring revenue about $500 million by March 2026, up from $285 million at the end of 2024
$7.5 billion in 2025, $8.4 billion in April 2026; about $1 billion raised in total

Texas directed at least $30 million in insurance-fee grants to local Flock networks before the governor halted the program in August 2026; Florida approved grant funding for about 440 readers shortly before its DOT revoked state right-of-way permits
Direct sales to individual agencies and communities; 404 Media published a Flock guide for police on presenting the product to councils; Flock offers pilot programs and grant-writing assistance
